sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: To ask for something in a shop, use kérek (I'd like / I ask for) followed by the noun with the accusative ending -t. The direct object — the thing you're asking for — always takes -t in Hungarian, unlike English where word order alone shows the object.
-t attaches directly after a linking vowel in kenyér → kenyeret, because kenyér is a front-vowel word ending in a consonant. You'll meet more of these patterns in the next lesson.
